text: The whole community of Israel set out from the wilderness of Sin, traveling by stages at the LORD's command, and camped at Rephidim. But there was no water for the people to drink.

versions.text: The whole community of Israel set out from the wilderness of Sin, moving on stage by stage at the LORD's command, and camped at Rephidim. But there was no water for the people to drink.
versions.explanation: "Moving on stage by stage" is slightly clumsy for oral reading and overlaps with "set out"; "traveling by stages" is smoother and equally accurate.

text: So the people quarreled with Moses and said, "Give us water to drink!" Moses answered them, "Why do you quarrel with me? Why do you put the LORD to the test?"
But the people were thirsty for water there, and they grumbled against Moses. "Why did you ever bring us up out of Egypt," they said, "to kill me and my children and my livestock with thirst?"

versions.text: But the people were thirsty for water there, and they grumbled against Moses. "Why did you ever bring us up out of Egypt," they said, "to kill us and our children and our livestock with thirst?"
versions.explanation: The Hebrew shifts to the singular voice of the people speaking as one ("to kill me and my children and my livestock"). Keeping the singular preserves the vivid, personal complaint; if the plural is retained for smoothness, a footnote noting the Hebrew singular would help.

text: Then Moses cried out to the LORD, "What am I to do with this people? A little more and they will stone me."
The LORD said to Moses, "Go on ahead of the people. Take some of the elders of Israel with you, and take in your hand the staff with which you struck the Nile, and go.
I will be standing there before you on the rock at Horeb. Strike the rock, and water will come out of it for the people to drink." So Moses did this in the sight of the elders of Israel.
He named the place Massah and Meribah, because the Israelites quarreled there and because they tested the LORD, saying, "Is the LORD among us or not?"
Then the Amalekites came and fought against Israel at Rephidim.
Moses said to Joshua, "Choose men for us and go out to fight against Amalek. Tomorrow I will stand on top of the hill with the staff of God in my hand."
Joshua did as Moses had told him and fought against Amalek, while Moses, Aaron, and Hur went up to the top of the hill.
As long as Moses held up his hand, Israel prevailed; but whenever he let his hand down, Amalek prevailed.
When Moses' hands grew heavy, they took a stone and put it under him, and he sat on it. Aaron and Hur held up his hands, one on each side, so that his hands remained steady until sunset.
So Joshua defeated Amalek and his people with the edge of the sword.

versions.text: So Joshua overwhelmed Amalek and his people with the sword.
versions.explanation: The verb חלש means to weaken, disable, or defeat; "overwhelmed" is an unusual rendering. Also לְפִי־חָרֶב is idiomatically "with the edge of the sword," which reads well aloud and preserves the image.

text: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Write this down in a book as a reminder, and make sure Joshua hears it: I will completely blot out the memory of Amalek from under heaven."
Moses built an altar and named it "The LORD Is My Banner."
He said, "A hand upon the throne of the LORD! The LORD will be at war against Amalek from generation to generation."

versions.text: He said, "A hand has been lifted to the throne of the LORD: the LORD is at war against Amalek from generation to generation."
versions.explanation: The Hebrew clause is verbless and notoriously difficult; "has been lifted" adds a verb not present. The war statement is also open-ended in Hebrew, so a future-oriented rendering fits "from generation to generation." A footnote noting the difficulty of the Hebrew phrase would be helpful.
